Across Africa, the energy revolution is accelerating. Investments in renewables have nearly tripled since 2019, and solar is now the least-cost source of power in most African markets.

This transformation holds immense opportunity. Africa possesses around 60% of the world’s best solar resources, yet only 1% of installed solar capacity. Unlocking this potential could power homes and industries, create over 3 million new green jobs by 2030, and drive inclusive growth from the ground up. But for this revolution to deliver lasting development impact, it must be just - anchored in governance, innovation, and digital empowerment.

1️⃣ Strengthen Governance
Establish transparent, accountable institutions with continent-wide standards for procurement, land use, and revenue sharing to ensure renewable wealth translates into jobs, community benefits, and public trust.

2️⃣ Mobilize Innovative Finance
Move from isolated projects to bankable investment pipelines. Blended finance, risk guarantees, and local-currency mechanism can de-risk markets and crowd in private capital. By mobilizing the estimated $190 billion per year needed by 2030, African countries can power inclusive industrialization and deliver universal energy access.

3️⃣ Harness Digital, Data & AI
Leverage AI and digital tools to make systems smarter and more affordable. Predictive analytics can cut project costs by 15%, and generative AI - if locally embedded in value chains - could unlock over $100 billion in annual economic value.

Africa’s energy revolution is not a story of scarcity but one of sovereign opportunity. With the right governance, finance, and digital backbone, the continent can transform its renewable wealth into sustainable development and true energy independence.
